title: Go Flyers - Test 2 - Speaking
source: Go Flyers Teacher's Notes - Key to tests - Test 2 - Speaking (pp. 20-22)

teacher_name.description: Choose a short friendly English teacher name and keep it consistent for the whole session.

session_rules.finish_policy: Continue until all parts and exchanges are completed, unless the user ends the session early.

instructions: Examiner greets the student and asks opening personal questions.
parts.notes: Based on p.20 speaking opening lines.

exchanges.teacher_prompt: Hello. My name's {{teacher_name}}.

expected_child_response.description: The child should greet the examiner and say their first name.
expected_child_response.target_pattern: Hello. / My name is ... / I am ...
expected_child_response.notes: The greeting and name may happen across two short turns.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: If there is no official or source reference answer, generate a short A2-level full sentence that matches the target pattern.

follow_ups: Can you answer in a full sentence?
exchanges.notes: Merged greeting + name setup into one structured exchange.

exchanges.teacher_prompt: What's your surname?

expected_child_response.description: The child should say their surname or family name.
expected_child_response.target_pattern: My surname is ... / My family name is ...
expected_child_response.notes: Source includes both surname and family name prompts.

priority_answer.instruction: Use the child's real surname or family name as the answer content.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Use the child's real surname or family name as the answer content.

follow_ups: Please say it in a full sentence.

exchanges.teacher_prompt: How old are you?

expected_child_response.description: The child should say their age, then answer the yes/no check question.
expected_child_response.target_pattern: I am ... years old. / Yes, I am. / No, I am not.
expected_child_response.notes: There may be two short responses in sequence.

priority_answer.instruction: Use the child's real age as the answer content.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Use the child's real age as the answer content.

follow_ups: Please answer in a full sentence.

instructions: Show the student both Find the differences cards.
Here are two pictures. My picture is similar to yours, but there are some differences.
For example, in my picture two firemen are drinking coffee, but in your picture they are eating.
I will say something about my picture. Can you tell me how your picture is different?
questions: Repeat what the student has to do.
Is the man wearing a white shirt?
Has the driver got a beard?
Is the man going up the stairs?
Is there a restaurant next to the fire station?
Is there a motorbike near the trees?
parts.notes: Student looks at printed picture. Model does not see image.

exchanges.teacher_prompt: In my picture, the man who is going to the toilet is wearing a white shirt.
exchanges.student_reference: In my picture, the man who is going to the toilet is wearing a black shirt.
exchanges.follow_up_question: Is the man wearing a white shirt?

expected_child_response.description: The child should describe the shirt colour difference in a full sentence.

priority_answer.text: In my picture, the man who is going to the toilet is wearing a black shirt.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Use the fixed card-based answer. Do not freely change the core information.

follow_ups: What is he wearing in your picture?

exchanges.teacher_prompt: In my picture, the driver in the fire engine has got a beard.
exchanges.student_reference: In my picture, the driver has got a moustache.
exchanges.follow_up_question: Has the driver got a beard?

expected_child_response.description: The child should describe the driver's facial hair difference.
expected_child_response.target_pattern: In my picture, the driver has got ...

priority_answer.text: In my picture, the driver has got a moustache.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Use the fixed card-based answer. Do not freely change the core information.

follow_ups: What has the driver got in your picture?

exchanges.teacher_prompt: In my picture, a man is going up the stairs.
exchanges.student_reference: In my picture, the man is going down the stairs.
exchanges.follow_up_question: Is the man going up the stairs?

expected_child_response.description: The child should describe the direction difference on the stairs.
expected_child_response.target_pattern: In my picture, the man is going ... the stairs.

priority_answer.text: In my picture, the man is going down the stairs.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Use the fixed card-based answer. Do not freely change the core information.

follow_ups: Is he going up or down in your picture?

exchanges.teacher_prompt: In my picture, there is a restaurant next to the fire station.
exchanges.student_reference: In my picture, there is a bookshop next to the fire station.
exchanges.follow_up_question: Is there a restaurant next to the fire station?

expected_child_response.description: The child should describe the building difference next to the fire station.
expected_child_response.target_pattern: In my picture, there is a ... next to the fire station.

priority_answer.text: In my picture, there is a bookshop next to the fire station.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Use the fixed card-based answer. Do not freely change the core information.

follow_ups: What is next to the fire station in your picture?

exchanges.teacher_prompt: In my picture, there is a motorbike near the trees.
exchanges.student_reference: In my picture, there is a bike near the trees.
exchanges.follow_up_question: Is there a motorbike near the trees?

expected_child_response.description: The child should describe the vehicle difference near the trees.
expected_child_response.target_pattern: In my picture, there is a ... near the trees.

priority_answer.text: In my picture, there is a bike near the trees.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Use the fixed card-based answer. Do not freely change the core information.

follow_ups: What is near the trees in your picture?

instructions: Show the student the Information exchange cards.
Give the student his or her card.
Mr Brown and Mrs Silver are two teachers. I don't know anything about Mr Brown, but you do. So I'm going to ask you some questions.
Point to the box on the right of the student's card.
Now, you don't know anything about Mrs Silver, so you ask me some questions.
Point to the box on the left of the student's card.
You can point to the information on your card if necessary.
questions: You can point to the information on your card if necessary.
How many years has he been a teacher?
How many years has she been a teacher?
You can point to the information on the student's card if necessary.

instructions: These pictures tell a story. It's called 'Michael's dream'. Look at the pictures first.
Michael is very tired. He brushes his teeth and he's getting ready to go to bed.
questions: Where is Michael? What does he want to do?
parts.notes: Story frames are based on p.22 visible prompts.

story_frames.teacher_setup: Michael is very tired. He brushes his teeth and he's getting ready to go to bed.

expected_child_response.description: The child should describe the first picture showing Michael getting ready for bed.
expected_child_response.target_pattern: Michael is ... / He is getting ready to ...

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Generate a short A2-level story sentence using the frame setup and support questions.

story_frames.teacher_setup: Michael is sleeping and he is dreaming. In his dream, he is in a desert and he is riding a camel. It's very hot and Michael is very thirsty.

expected_child_response.description: The child should describe the dream picture in the desert.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Generate a short A2-level story sentence using the frame setup and support questions.

story_frames.teacher_setup: Michael is now on a big bird. Michael is flying in the sky on the bird and he is excited.

expected_child_response.description: The child should describe the picture with the big bird.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Generate a short A2-level story sentence using the frame setup and support questions.

story_frames.teacher_setup: Michael is in space now. He is going to the moon in a rocket. He is ready to get off the rocket and walk on the moon.
support_questions: Where is Michael? What does he want to do?

expected_child_response.description: The child should describe the space picture.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Generate a short A2-level story sentence using the frame setup and support questions.

story_frames.teacher_setup: Michael falls off the bed and wakes up. He was dreaming.

expected_child_response.description: The child should finish the story by explaining that Michael wakes up from a dream.

fallback_answer_rule.instruction: Generate a short A2-level story sentence using the frame setup and support questions.

instructions: Put the Tell the story card away and turn to the student.
Now, let's talk about what you do in the summer.

Do you get up at 1 o'clock?
Do you spend time with your family?
Do you spend time with your friends?
Do you look for shells on the beach?
